utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Tadic, Simo Zaric, and Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination is continuing with Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all the present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're going to continue where we left off on Friday. My last question had to do with, if you remember, the Cafe AS, and we stopped when I asked you when the last time was that you entered Cafe AS. You said this was in November 1991. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you the following question now: Do you maybe remember that in March or April 1992, you entered Cafe AS and that you were there together with Mr. Izet Izetbegovic and Stevo, nicknamed Kocka?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you're not sure, just please say so. Just say, "I don't remember."

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you personally see some people in uniform entering the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These were SMB uniforms, as you described them on Friday?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, SMB uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also said, on the 28th of May, that your people informed you on the fact that the Grey Wolves were also patronising Cafe AS.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did these people, informers of yours, your collaborators from within the 4th Detachment, personally enter the Cafe AS to observe these things or would they observe or monitor from the outside who was entering Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were members of the 4th Detachment, they observed the events from the inside, and those that were not, those who were members of the before-mentioned units, they would do it from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what you said. Did these people who were members of the 4th Detachment tell you that the Grey Wolves entered AS or did the people from the patrols tell you this fact?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were in AS, that is to say, members of the 4th Detachment, and people who were in the units also said that the same were also at the Memorial Centre Mitra Trifunovic Uco, that that's where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These Grey Wolves, were they in uniform when they were in the Cafe AS? What did your people tell you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time they were wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you roughly tell me when this was in relation to April 17th? How much time before the 17th were they seen?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were seen in March of 1992, when they arrived by helicopter to the local commune Batkusa, whose majority population was Serb, that is to say, mostly Serbs inhabit this place, and they came there by helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to follow up on a question asked by Judge Williams on the 28th of May, when she wanted to know about the identity of these people from the 4th Detachment. You said that at the beginning you had two informers in the 4th Detachment, that is to say, your people that were members of the 4th Detachment, and that later there were about ten of them.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Considering the fact that this is hearsay, I would like you -- I would have to insist that you give us the names of the people who confirmed this fact. And if the Prosecutor insists, we can go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The first thing is, if we are going to get into this information, I think we'd have to go into closed session. I don't know if these people are living in Bosanski Samac, and if they are, it could be a problem for them. Then assuming this is admissible, I think certain restrictions are going to have to be placed. We can't have Mr. Zaric discussing this matter with his wife and then his wife approaching people or telling people in Bosanski Samac, as we've had in previous situations, about what's going on. We're going to have to set up some restrictions on this information, if it is admissible. I would also request that - although I'm not cross-examining - that we should at least begin by looking to see who the patrol people were, if you recall, that saw this, and maybe the informants would just be cumulative. But that's really up to the Court. And finally, counsel is insisting on the information. That's not for counsel to insist. Counsel can request. The Court can order the witness to answer, not counsel, because counsel is saying he insists on these answers. That's not for counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's a question of language, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Then we can go into closed session because you mentioned that you don't know whether these people are still in Bosanski Samac, where they are actually living. So to be on the safe side, let's go into closed session. Yes, private session, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you are aware of the fact that cards were played at Cafe AS.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That people from all over the former Yugoslavia would come there to play cards, from Serbia, Slovenia, Croatia? Do you know of this or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just before the war, in April 1992, people gambled in Cafe AS, and those were also members of the Grey Wolves that came to Batkusa by helicopter. They also gambled there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did your informers, or I should say maybe collaborators, tell you that your party colleagues, Omer Nalic and Izet Izetbegovic, also frequently patronised the cafe and also your fellow townsperson Hasan Bicic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as Hasan Bicic and Omer Nalic are concerned, it's probably true. They were more frequent patrons than Izet Izetbegovic. I don't know if Izet Izetbegovic came there a lot. But the first two, yes, Nalic and Bicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was whether you heard about this from your informers.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember or do you know that on the Sit building, which is across Cafe AS -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That from January 1992 until the beginning of the hostilities, there was a flag of Bosnia-Herzegovina and a flag of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the very same day you answered, when asked by the Prosecutor, that the location of the Cafe AS was a good one, a good choice, because this part of town was inhabited mainly by Serbs. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that right next to AS, that in this building there is also a Croatian and a Muslim family residing?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this building right next to Cafe AS. There's also a supermarket there. Yes, the owner of this building is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the first building on the right when you're facing the entrance of AS, this was a building where a Croatian family lived?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, behind the Cafe AS there were 6.000 Serb houses and a hundred Croat and Muslim houses, so what was exactly around AS or around ten metres, it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, my question was very specific. If you do not know, you do not know.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered you. The building next to Cafe AS is owned by a man who is a Croat. I even know his name: Bozo Breskackovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in this so-called Novo Naselje that you mentioned, and you said that trucks were being unloaded -- the truck was being unloaded there, do you know that Sulejman Tihic had his truck there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the very beginning of Novo Naselje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And his brother as well?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And also Jusuf Jusufovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, there were about 500 houses there, and you are now listing three or four examples. In the previous question, I told you that there were 6.000 people that lived behind these objects.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Fitozovic, please, let's speed up. I heard what you said, but my question is very specific. Could you just please say "yes" or "no." Everything that you said entered into the record, so you do not have to repeat yourself twice.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you don't have to ask me the same question more than once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, remember to pause. Mr. Fitozovic, just answer the questions as they come. If counsel asks twice or three times the same question, just answer it. If the Prosecution finds that it's not -- what counsel is doing is not proper, the Prosecution will intervene. If the Trial Chamber finds that the questioning is not proper, the Trial Chamber will intervene. So when there is no intervention, please just answer the questions as they come.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have one more question that has to do with the owners of these houses surrounding Cafe AS. Did Asim Delic and Zaimbegovic Zaim also have houses there? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the names?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Zaim Zaimbegovic and Asim Delic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how about Cafe Molla? This was a place that you patronised frequently?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And mostly Muslims gathered here. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Croats as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The owner of this cafe was Ratif Atic? Rajec?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ratif.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but his nickname is Rajec; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This was a man who you gave a position inside your TO organisational structure?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there a single Serb house in the close proximity of that cafe?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How close?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifty metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the majority of the houses are Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In front of this cafe, three members of the 4th Detachment were severely wounded?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on to another topic. Mr. Fitozovic, you were a reserve officer in the old JNA?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just for the record, could they state the names of the people who were wounded so we're not thinking that there were several battles that were going on in front of that cafe, so we're all talking about the same people. Are we talking about the Tota Danilo incident?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was of the same view, whether it's the same people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just to keep the record clear, otherwise people can argue there were also incidents that were occurring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Lukic can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question that had to do with the injuring in front of the Cafe Molla had to do with the incident that you described that happened in March, where Tota and some other persons belonging to the 4th Detachment were wounded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also said, as far as I can remember, that you had military training at least twice a month while you were a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume that you remember well that in every call to attend a military training, it was said that if you failed to come, if you failed to accept the invitation, that there would be some kind of a penalty.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that these things could cause you to be penalised.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another consequence -- the same consequence applied to the reserve corps of the JNA and the TO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this Territorial Defence that you organised in 1992, in April, people volunteered to join; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you did not force anybody to join the TO?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And all these people that volunteered, they knew that they were members of the TO, but they did not know what kind of duties they would have?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They had no time to find out because the aggression took place in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In these lists that we saw on Friday, I noticed phone numbers. Could you please tell me where you got the phone numbers of these people from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the survey, on the questionnaire, there was a column called "Phone, Home, and Work Phone," so the people that filled out the questionnaire themselves filled out these facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So these people volunteered this information?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am also interested in this self-organised unit of citizens that you described that was organised in autumn of 1991, and according to the number, it had about 212 members. Did people also volunteer to join this unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So nobody was in any way forced or coerced to become a member of this self-organised unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would ask you now to enter the private session because we will be moving to a topic where some names shall be mentioned which requested protection, people who requested protection. It will be very short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to discuss with the witness a certain document, a document which has been disclosed to the Prosecution. I would like to ask the usher to bring forward the document. It is a document why ... I would kindly ask for an identification number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have a number for identification only, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D50/3 ter and D50/3 for the English translation. Thank you. Just to add, ID, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, have you seen this document earlier?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've already spoken of it in your statement to the Prosecution in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My first question: What is the city command of Bosanski Samac at the time? What was that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know what my rights are, and can I be assisted here before answering this question? Can the Prosecutor assist me here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What type of assistance do you need? You've been asked a question by the counsel: What is the city command of Bosanski Samac at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would only like to say something about this very document, and I need assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What type of assistance? What's the problem with giving the answer that counsel is demanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I did bring the original. It was a -- just by chance. This is the original, and this is a forgery. On the forgery, we do have a signature here; on the original, we do not have it. This is the original of the communication, and it was submitted to this Trial Chamber as exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. All right. So you have the original document, which is containing the information, and you'd like the original document to be produced. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Maybe we can facilitate this. Could we place this up on a table and all counsel can come and look at it and make a quick comparison? It will take about a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one? The document that the witness is saying --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. The two of them, if we could place them right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The usher can give what the witness is showing as an original to counsel to look at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the original stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that the original you are discussing, Mr. Fitozovic, is in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we can have that document also given a number. Yes. Can we look at it? Maybe can we have an ID number for the document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D51/3 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, since the document is very fragile, seems like it's falling apart, can it be placed in plastic for safety?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the usher can assist with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we have a clarification, Your Honours, please? Is it D51/3? It's produced by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I'm discussing with the Judges, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm running ahead. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are of the view that it should have a "P" number, a Prosecution number. Can we just correct that, please? For identification only.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be P67 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I start with my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We want to look at what the witness says is the original, which is now P67 ter ID. Yes. Counsel can go ahead with the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The defendants have asked for the original document to be put on the ELMO so that they can also take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It can be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, you claim that you have the original document, D50/3 [sic] ter?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. This is the original document that I swam the river Sava with. It was original. It was put in a freezer bag for food.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you the following: Is it the practice of all institutions that had communications with other institutions that the copy remaining with the person -- the one that is not being sent, was it the custom that that copy not be signed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it's obvious that this is a forgery. I do not understand this. I don't know anything about correspondence law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that it was a custom that those documents that would stay in the archives of your party not be signed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the copies have to be signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive this document from the TO, or was this a copy that was at the SDA headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When you are talking about -- since we have this dispute about the original and the other documents, can we be specific, now that we have numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document D51/3, did you receive this document at the TO staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Which one is D51? We gave it a Prosecution number, meaning the original. It's P67 ter ID. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. I apologise. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the document P67 ter ID, is this the document that you got at the TO headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So where do you have this document from, then?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my document. What do you mean, where I got it from? I have it. It's the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you write it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm the author of the upper part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the lower part where the stamp is and where there's no signature, you didn't write that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, actually, I think I would just like to see what the witness calls the original back here again, just for one moment, because I want to look at the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: When this comes back on the ELMO, I've noticed that the stamp is at a different angle on the original. On the original -- hard to explain. One has to see it. But it's tilted to the right, with the letters on a diagonal from upper left to lower right. On the copy that we have, it's -- yes, D50/3 ter ID, it's exactly straight, the stamp. So it's different on both. And this has nothing to do with the crease in the paper of what the witness has produced to us. So the two do seem to be different, although saying the same thing. The stamps, they're at different angles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to ask counsel if for the record they could tell us from where they have obtained that document, or if it violates attorney client privilege, they don't have to answer that. But since we're looking at what is potentially a forged document, could they tell us where they got it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean D50/3 ter?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the one we are look at is actually a photocopy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. The photocopy the witness claims to be -- or have a forgery on it, could they tell us where they received that document? Or if it's going to violate attorney-client privilege, they don't have to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to be hard for me to get my turn. I fully understood what Judge Williams said. We could not have submitted the copy that was with the witness. We have the original of the document that we are going to tender now as evidence. This is the original that was found at the TO headquarters, and this is a document that the TO staff received from the command of the town, and that is the document that we are tendering. And then I would like to talk to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you -- when you are talking about, that is the document we are tendering, what's the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is document D50/3 ter ID. This is the document whose copies you have and I'm going to submit also the original, and there is a signature and a stamp of the authorised person in the SDA. This is not a forgery. And we are going to prove this in the further proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have the Judges be shown this original first. Your Honours, the original of the document that I showed you, D50/3 ter ID, and the document -- this is the document that has been disclosed to the Prosecution as well. The document that the witness has is a copy of the document, but this was not the document that was found in the premises of the TO staff in Bosanski Samac, and this is what the Defence will prove in its case. It is obvious that the copy that the witness has is an unsigned copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Once you say the copy that the witness has, give it a number, please. There will be less confusion that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. The document that the witness has, P67 ter ID, the witness said that he was the author of the first part of that document, and this is an unofficial document. That's why there is no signature. The document with the signature of the authorised person in the town council of SDA is the official document that was found at the TO staff, because it was communicated -- this was a document that was sent to the TO staff, and that's why it was found there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, I would like to ask you the following:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- oh, you are still looking at the -- yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I approach counsel? Because the one that we have, the copy, is different from the so-called original. There's a "17" listed on this original, and the "7" -- there's a "7" which is over a "3." The one I have has "13." There's also a "06" with several slash marks, which doesn't exist on this original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can approach counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. Yes, I was just about to say, I don't think that should be a problem that should hold us, because each party will make their submissions on the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. I will just say for the future, what they did is they put -- internally, they put some markings on documents, and if something is an original, you should not write on the document, because it raises questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: They wrote a "13" on it, then they crossed out the "3" and then wrote a "7" on it. But that's an original. They should just use it different method of protecting originals than writing on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. That is noted. Yes, Mr. Lukic. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, the parties will talk about the authenticity of this document, but we will just discuss the contents of the document right now. You have already said that you are the author of the first portion of this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number D50/3 ter ID. That's the document that I'm talking about right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But this is -- I thought that this is the document D50/3 ID. This is the document the witness has already said is a forgery, and then he produced the one in the plastic, I think P67 ter ID, which he says is the original, which he -- according to him, he wrote the first part. I thought that was the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is his position. But I'm talking about the same document, D50/3 ter ID and P67. But I would like also to have my document, the document that I'm saying is the original, be put on the file. That's D50/3. That's the one that has the signature; as opposed to the document P67 that does not have a signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So you want it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted it to be stated that this copy also has a number or that it be -- or that the same number be used for the other document, for the record. The original of the D50/3, I'm tendering right now. Whether it will get a separate number or not, I'm not -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's just -- when we get photocopies for use, they are given a number. So the original retains the same number, because it's the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could you please put the other document also on the ELMO. Yes, both.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, we are now talking about this document that has the number P -- D50/3 ter ID as well as P67 ter. Could we agree that the difference between the two documents lies in the fact that D50/3 ter ID is signed and the other one is not signed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you were the author of the first portion of the contents of the documents, of these two documents.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this first part --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I must intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The witness answered "yes" on the first question, and in transcript it's "no." So maybe we could clarify that with the witness. The question was, page 33, line 9, and his answer is in line 13. In transcript, there is a "no" as his answer, but he said "yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we go back with the witness, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Fitozovic, let's just repeat my question and your answer. Would you agree that the difference between these two documents lies in the fact, and only in the fact, that D50/3 ter has a signature in the part where it says "SDA town board, Bosanski Samac," whereas document P67 ter ID does not have a signature?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter note. If the witness could please come closer to the microphone. It was hard to hear him.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree, but we have to say that the stamp of SDA on the 17th of April, 1992 was at the police or in some other institution. So starting from the 16th of April, this stamp was no longer in the possession of the Party of Democratic Action. So after that, many documents all of a sudden had this stamp of SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the paper that you had with you, that went with you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document that I had with me, that's the original, Mr. Lukic, because you can see that there is no signature here by the command of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Experts will be making comparisons about what the differences are.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that the original does not have the signature. The original without the signature, that's exactly the problem: Who was supposed to sign on behalf of the command of the town and who was supposed to sign on behalf of the town board. That's why there was no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I continue with my questioning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was just worried about the overlapping, because you didn't allow the witness to complete his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what this institution was, the town command of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The town command of Bosanski Samac was exactly that list of self-organised and unarmed citizens that was created in October or November of 1991. This is when the citizens organised themselves when they could see that the 4th Detachment was organised, and other detachments around Bosanski Samac, and when units came from Serbia and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You already answered this. Could you please be brief.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the town command, the command of all citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what is this list of self-organised citizens doing in the town board of SDA? In the last part here, it says: "We please ask you to submit the same list for your disposal."

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This list of self-organised citizens of Bosanski Samac, the Party of Democratic Action verified this list, because based on the order of the presidency and the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we had the duty to do this and to address all of those who had illegal or legal weapons that was not licenced anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you call this institution the command of the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It was comprised of all citizens of the town of Bosanski Samac, and later, then it was also on the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And this list was kept in the town board of SDA? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you are the author of this text?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the author of the text. But you're asking me about the list now. I am the author of this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I can notice - and you can tell me if I'm wrong or not - in the second part, it says here that the list of persons is also given to the disposal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is on --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before the witness answers, that is on which document? Is it P67 or D50?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On both documents. I'm going to ask the witness to read slowly the last paragraph, but slowly, so that the Trial Chamber and the interpreters can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this is the paragraph that is below the date.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the request of the command of town of Bosanski Samac, we hereby forward their memorandum of 13th of April, 1992, received by the party from the town command on the 14th of April, 1992, with a request to send it to you with the list." "SDA, Party of Democratic Action, town board," signature forged, and stamp of SDA, that the occupier helped themselves with later, after the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The last thing you said, is this your comment or is this written here?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I only asked you to read what was written here, and I didn't want there to be any mistake.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is with regard to D50/3 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lukic. Before your next question, I just wonder if you could -- if you look at your question, on page 36, lines 5 to 7, I don't quite understand - and maybe it's just the translation - where you say -- well, you say: As far as I can notice - you can tell me if I'm wrong or not - in the second part, it says that the list of persons is also given to the disposal; is that correct?" And the witness says "yes." "Disposal," I just don't understand what the question means in the English version here. It seems to be also an important question, and the witness answered "yes." So if you could maybe think back to your original in your own language, that would be useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like your assistance. I do not see the laptop in front of me, so that I cannot see that record and I cannot see what -- okay. I see that a colleague of mine is trying to help me here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: It was lines 5 to 7 on page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter note. The counsel quoted the last part of the document, "with a request to send it to you with the list."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I give the clarification, Your Honour? It's the second part of the document, which is now on the ELMO. And in fact the question was: "The second part of this document says that the list of persons is also given to the..." for the use or for the knowledge or something like that, in that sense, in Serbian language, that was the question. But obviously it's related to the second part of this document, where the SDA Town Board attached this list to first letter and then sent to TO for the further - I don't know - use or something like that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Pantelic. That explains. And also thank you for the interpreter for your comment on the same note.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, in this part that you said you were the author of, there is a sentence that I'm very interested in. You quoted that you're part -- you're the author of the text in the last part of the communication. That refers to the legally and illegally procured weapons. What was your opinion -- what was your position, so that you put this in?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is a fact witness. I realise he said this, but I don't think he should be offering his legal conclusions to this Court why he said this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think he can explain it, because he says -- he has said he's the author. He can explain it, even though he's a fact witness, because it happens to be something he himself offered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the counsel can ask in what sense did he mean, because he does -- he does say a combination of legally and illegally procured weapons. So that -- this is different from the general issues of legality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see, this document was sent to the municipal staff of Territorial Defence, and here I wanted to point out that our weapons do exist, for which individuals of the Territorial Defence had possession and lawfully owned it. They had the permits of the municipal authorities. And when I said as far as illegally procured weapons, then I wanted to indicate, Mr. Lukic, that the 30 rifles which were procured privately, and another 20 which were also procured privately, and that that be placed under the control of the TO. And once the Territorial Defence was formed, I wasn't interested any more in persons who were in possession of legal weapons. And with this communication, I want to make it public that it be registered with the official authority, the official body, TO, and the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we're going to be over our time too break. It's 10.34. We'll take our break now and resume our proceedings at 11.05.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The last question concerning this document, I don't know whether I concluded correctly from your last answer, and explain it to me. Does this mean, when I asked you what was considered as legal weapons and/or illegal weapons, that you considered as illegal weapons those weapons which you procured and which you described earlier, the supply from that truck which broke down, the explosive, the 30 rifles? Do you consider that illegal weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not illegal, but weapons procured illegally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that your answer as you wrote it --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me be clear. In a way --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. I think he's answered the question and I think the more we go into this, you're asking him to make legal decisions or offer legal conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think -- yes. The answer was complete, in my view. Weapons procured illegally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I have no other submissions in connection with this document, and I propose that document D50/3 ter ID and that this be submitted as official evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean you want D50/3 ter and the English version submitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would ask that the Court wait until after re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have some questions about that document, and see what the answers are, what further discussion we have in relation to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So they will be submitted -- the question -- the Prosecution's position will be we'll go back to them after re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour. And now I would pass on to the next document. I would ask the usher -- this is the document which was disclosed

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, the document does not have an official translation. I submitted it for translation on the 17th of April. It is -- some of the documents I received, and their translations, but not this one. I would kindly ask the witness to read it slowly. It is also a document of which the witness already spoke with the Prosecution, although I'm not quite sure. Could we receive the identification number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D51/3 ter ID, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, I would kindly ask you to read this document, but slowly, as we do not have an English translation, from the heading onwards, sir. Maybe it would be easier for you to read from the copy in front of you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Municipality Bosanski Samac. Municipal staff of Territorial Defence. Number 01/39-1. Date, 16th, 4th, April, 1992." In the upper right corner: "Military secret. Strictly confidential."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I must intervene, Your Honours. Page 42, line 2, it's not clear, 16th and 4th. We have to make a correction to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Yes. Can we have the date again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Date, 16.04.1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Communication-submitted to the republican staff of TO, Sarajevo." "We are informing you that on the 15.04.1992, the staff of TO of the municipality of Bosanski Samac has been established, and which is expressing its loyalty to the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and will submit itself under the control of the TO staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. "Up until the present day, we have registered on our list of soldiers in our unit, and volunteers, 1.800. "We have at our disposal only some 400 barrels (infantry weapons)." "Financial means for the functioning of the TO staff have not been ensured at the level of the municipality because the financing of the Municipal Assembly in the hands of the opposing forces." Further below to the left: "Drafted in (2)," in brackets, "two writing, two copies, and addressees, copy number 1, to the republican staff of TO SRBH; copy 2, the archives, the file of the municipality SDO." And below, right-hand corner, "Commander Captain Marko Bozanovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thank you. Are you acquainted with this document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, was this document drafted and signed by the commander Bozanovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this document reflect the true situation as it was at the time of its drafting?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, pausing. We have the same person, question and answer, interpreting. Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as these abbreviations go, in the second line, we have "V/O." These are soldiers. And in the last conscript, and what -- "SO" in the last -- "SO" in the last line, that is the assembly of the municipality. Can you tell me from this document: It turns out that you had registered 1.800 members, but here that you had -- and the conscripts and the volunteers. Why is there a distinction which is being drawn between these two terms?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can explain it to you in the following manner: This document was produced on the date which it bears, when also other -- the local communes submitted their list to the TO staff. As that previous document with the city command submitted a communication to the staff of Territorial Defence. So the document exists which states where also the other local communes submitted their list of their conscripts. And as far as this distinction between the conscripts and volunteers, the distinction, the difference, is in the following: That everybody, depending on their age, did not belong in that category of conscripts but signed up as volunteers. For example, maybe these were people who were over 60, 65.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I fully agree. But from this answer you've given us, this number 1.000 -- this 800 [sic] applies only to Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From this, it clearly -- it is clear. When we say that we're informing you that on the 15th, 04, 1992, the staff of TO was founded. Mr. Lukic, I'm answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The record won't make sense. Allow the witness to complete the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I can see that because you understand the language, and you're not agreeing with him, so you intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I forgot that you have no English translation in front of you. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And also, the record has to make sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So read this sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is, from the first sentence, you can see we are informing you that on the 15th, 04, 1992, the TO staff was formed, staff of Territorial Defence, of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, its municipality, and not the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understood that. And the volunteers, they didn't have this obligation as the conscripts had?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The volunteers were those people whose age exceeded the legal limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The conscripts also applied their own free will, voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, also on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not need this document any more and I will move on to another subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm sure you are aware that you've exceeded the one and-a-half hours already. I hope had you are coming to a close, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam President, I am fully aware of that. We are discussing just a single document for 45 minutes, and I certainly didn't expect that we would have three different copies of that document. I'll try to wind up as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, at the end of the examination-in-chief, you described what your tasks were after swimming across the river in the municipality of Odzak. I think you can give us some information about Odzak. On the 5th, 6th, 7th of May, in Odzak, negotiations were under way, under the auspices of the international observers, concerning the encircled Serbs in the town?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those dates, I was not on the territory of the municipality of Odzak, and I know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have information that you, as a representative of HVO, were present at these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your information is erroneous.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you have no information about the incarceration of Serbs in Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume you knew quite well Marko Bozanovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know Mijo Matanovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what was the function of this person and his role?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which person?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to Mijo Matanovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period you're referring to, I don't know what Mijo Matanovic was doing at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And for what period you do know what his function was and his activity was?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've known him during the period of July, when I visited him and requested that my wife and children be allowed to move from Bosanski Samac because their lives were being threatened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please answer me. What was that person? What was his function? Why did you go there? Mijo Matanovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked on exchanges, and I've known him since July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For whom did he work on the question of exchange? Did he work for the Serbian, Croatian, or the Muslim side? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time he worked for the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we are discussing July 1992? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was a member of the Exchange Commission of HVO for Bosnian Posavina? Do you know that? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The two of us understand each other, but also the Trial Chamber must understand what we're saying. You also mentioned during the examination-in-chief to the Prosecutor that you were present at the exchanges which took place between the Croatian and the Yugoslav side in the town of Samac, and you also said that, among other things, this also created a poor climate in the relations.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we seem to have a bit of a problem. Counsel is asking a question, he's answering a question. By the time they finish the question, get to his answer, counsel is starting the next question. I have no opportunity to object if there's something objectionable. They've got to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic and Mr. Fitozovic, please do pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, in 1991 and up until the outbreak of conflict, how many exchanges took place in Samac, to your recollection, and if you remember when these exchanges took place?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the exchanges did take place at the municipality of Bosanski Samac, in Bosanski Samac itself, and the number of exchanges was, as far as I know, three or four.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that they all took place at the end of 1991? When was the last exchange? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender another document in connection with this. It is the document -- an article from the paper Oslobodjenje from the 10th of November, 1991, which describes the exchange which took place in Samac. I have also an official translation. And this has also been submitted to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Has the Prosecution seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. It was supplied to us last week. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have it as an exhibit? Can we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D52/3 for the English translation and D52/3 ter for the B/C/S version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to correct my learned colleague of the Prosecution. I disclosed this document in September of 2001 to the Prosecution. Last week, I reminded him that I would be using this document after I heard what the witness had to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read, Mr. Fitozovic, this document? I would like to ask you a number of questions about it. The daily Oslobodjenje, where was it being published? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the territory of the entire Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where was it published?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the territory of the entire Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was where the headquarters of this news agency was.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of the entire Yugoslavia, there were bureaus of Oslobodjenje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the seat of Oslobodjenje in Sarajevo? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the exchange that took place in Bosanski Samac on November 9th, 1991, between Croatia and the Yugoslav side?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I remember this exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who came from the Croatian side and who went to the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One part of the war detainees from east Slavonia went to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Members of the Croatian army that were caught by the JNA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And to the territory of the then SFRY, or Bosnia-Herzegovina, do you remember who went there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During these exchanges, do you remember that people who were exchanged and who would go to the Croatian side across the bridge on the river Sava, that they were not taken to the town of Samac, that they were taken instead directly to the bridge?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were taken to the area where today the free customs area is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the playground in the centre, members and soldiers of the JNA and other persons that were coming from Croatia and going towards Bosnia-Herzegovina, were placed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not bring them hamburgers?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have one short topic. I wanted to read portions of this document with this witness.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it doesn't say here that they were at the stadium. I don't know where they were. How can you claim that they were at the stadium?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is whether you knew that on the playground by the primary school, buses with people from Croatia were put and that those people later would go towards Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have only a few more questions about a very brief subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you answered questions of the Prosecution, and also of Mr. Pisarevic, you described your return from Prud in the early morning hours, around 4.00. You said to the Prosecutor: "Then I found myself there with my men." Do you remember this? When you crossed the bridge from Prud to Samac and you arrived in Samac in the early hours.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, at 4.30, I was not in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. At 9.30. It was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 9.30, I met my men.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is as follows: At that time did you also meet Ibrahim Salkic, nicknamed Ibela? Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you meet Kemal Mehinovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you meet the brothers Dagovic, Esad and Safet?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I can tell you who I met with. I met with Ivica Dzebic, who at that time told me that his brother was killed. A pistol was put in his mouth and that's how he was killed. And I also met Zeljko Sedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you met nobody else?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pasaga Tihic was also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have one further question as part of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show the witness a map. Just a moment. Actually, I have here with me map D49/3, and I would like the witness to indicate where these locations were, for example, the office where he was hiding and so on, where he was hiding the first night. He said that this was, as far as I can remember, in Marsal Tito Street. I might be wrong about this, though.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, may I just call your attention to the fact that D49/3 is a ter document. It's actually a list of exchanged people. D49/3 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. There are two marks, because we tendered it twice. The basic number is D27/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a map, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. You just said on the record a map D49/3. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tendered this map the first time when it was given the number D27/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, my question will be very short. If you could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you just wait? I'm wondering whether the map given to the witness -- the one on the ELMO, is that from the registry? Is that the copy from the registry or is it a clean copy which you intend to use of the -- yes. Let's just get this clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registrar can also see that this is a clean copy, and I would like the witness to indicate where he was hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have in front of you a marker, Mr. Fitozovic, and I would like to ask you, if you could, to indicate on this map where was the office where you were hiding in? And then from there, you went to the Usce building. What street was it in? And could you please put a dot where it is, and if you could, a number 1 right next to it.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is Marsala Tito Street, near -- ?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The city library.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And also near the bridge over the river Bosna, towards Prud; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you left this area because a shell fell nearby.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you indicate where this shell was -- where the shell hit? Could you please put a dot there as well.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the shell came from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came from the direction of Skaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How would you know this?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it because these shells flew over my head, and they weren't falling in this location here; they were falling across the river Sava. Not a single shell fell in this location here. They were all falling towards Sava and over the river Sava, and it was obvious that this one fell too short.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it is your claim that this shell came from the side that was under the control of the Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please indicate with a number 3 where you hid next. Where are these premises of Usce?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This isn't really a good map, but here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please put number 3 there.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the premises of Usce Bosne, and also a residential area owned by the family Dzakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to state for the record that the witness, under 1, showed the law firm where he was on the 17th of April; under number 2, the location where the shell fell that, by his word, came from Skaric; and under 3, he identified the building where he went to next.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And these are the premises of the Usce Bosne company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Usce Bosne, and also the family home of Dzakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, and I would like an ID for this document. And I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You want it an exhibit in your case, isn't it, Mr. Lukic, this map which Mr. Fitozovic has just marked? Because you said you wanted an ID number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I would like to tender it. It can get a full mark. The problem is that the basic map that has the name of -- has the number of D27/3 has an ID number because we're not convinced yet of its authenticity, whereas this map that he has put his marks on right now can be an evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because what I noticed was that the witness had no problem identifying the various places you wanted him to mark. Any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection. If he wants and the witness can say this is a valid map, we can put both of them in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not really. It's just that the witness has marked it and the Prosecution has no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The registrar would like to make it clear for the record that the map marked by witness -- previous witness Esad Dagovic, on the 13th of February, it was admitted on the 18th of February, so it's no longer an ID document. It's D27/3 ter document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. So this one, what's the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D53/3, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: If I could just clarify with the registry assistant. You said it was admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have it done as admitted on the 18th of February, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. It's just my recollection there was some controversy at that time with that witness, but if that's correct, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I can check the record in the meanwhile, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to remind the Trial Chamber that I tendered this document during the cross-examination of Esad Dagovic -- actually, this is how I remember it. And then he made some comments on some buildings and he said that the map was not accurate. And therefore, I said that I would try to make sure to get an opinion about how authentic and true the map is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I also said that some of the buildings here were not quite accurately located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think that is on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Prior to beginning, Your Honours, allow me to just make a quick reference to the issue with regard to the way of examination of the witness, which was firstly made by this Trial Chamber on the 18th of October, 2001, page 2524, 2525. And then a quote of Madam President of this Bench, 7th of November, 2001, page 3643. In brief, I just want to make this reference to my learned friends because I don't want to be interrupted by the way how I will make my cross-examination. I don't want to have any kind of objection with regard to the coaching of this witness. And finally, everything is clear. I have -- and I will put to this witness certain events, certain facts, according to the instruction of this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Pantelic. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because I'm entitled to do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Fitozovic. My name is Pantelic. I am the trial attorney of Mr. Blagoje Simic. Could you please turn on the microphone that is in front of you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you visit Blagoje Simic and his family?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you ever patronise restaurants with him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe we had a drink here and there.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please make a pause before asking the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you remember to pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Allow the answer to be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are a witness that, from October to, say, March -- October 1991, March 1992, there was a lot of effort to find a peaceful solution, both by the international community and all the institutions in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: These activities had to do with the Lisbon Agreement in February 1991, where all three parties, political parties, participated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. The Lisbon Agreement, and all the other ones, you could have asked other witnesses about this. I couldn't really tell you much about this, or in any detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you find out about these things through the media or through your party membership?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, through the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that on the level of the municipality, between the three coalition partners - SDA, SDA, and HDZ - there have also been some talks going on that had to do with the implementation of a possible agreement and things like that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I was asking you whether you have any knowledge that they talked about these issues.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were present when the SDA in Samac created its town board; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
